notes: Bundibugyo virus identified by INRB; cases span 13 health zones across Ituri / Nord-Kivu / Sud-Kivu provinces (Ituri remains epicenter; Sud-Kivu first lab-confirmed case 2026-05-25). CDC Travel Notice escalated from Level 2 to Level 3 after the 2026-05-16 CDC Situation Summary publication. US State Department Travel Advisory at Level 4 (Do Not Travel) for DRC; US entry restrictions in effect from 2026-05-22 on non-US passport holders who travelled to DRC in the previous 21 days, extended to green-card holders the same week; CDC Title 42 Order in effect for arrivals from DRC (https://www.cdc.gov/media/releases/2026/statement-update-on-title-42-order.html). US arrivals from affected countries funneled through IAD (from 2026-05-21), ATL (from 2026-05-22), and IAH Houston (from 2026-05-26) for enhanced screening. On 2026-05-31 the DRC government and WHO issued a joint statement explicitly asking other governments to keep borders open (https://www.who.int/news/item/31-05-2026-joint-statement-by-the-government-of-the-democratic-republic-of-the-congo-and-who-concerning-the-outbreak-of-ebola-disease-caused-by-the-bundibugyo-virus). 2026-06-15: CDC re-reviewed the DRC Level 3 notice (page now dated 15 June 2026); the affected provinces (Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu) remain Level 3 (Reconsider Nonessential Travel), with non-affected DRC provinces now covered under the combined DRC+Uganda Level 2 notice (https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices/level2/ebola-drc-uganda). DRC Level 3 URL and level unchanged. 2026-07-12: the DRC Institut National de Sante Publique formally designated Haut-Uele and Tshopo as epidemic zones (4 cases including 2 deaths in Tshopo, 1 death in Haut-Uele, all judged imported from Nia Nia HZ in Ituri), taking the outbreak from 3 to 5 affected provinces (Reuters via CNBC Africa https://www.cnbcafrica.com/2026/congo-says-ebola-outbreak-spreads-to-provinces-haut-uele-and-tshopo). CDC has NOT re-scoped its Level 3 notice, which still names only Ituri, Nord-Kivu and Sud-Kivu; watch for a re-scope. 2026-07-15: CDC re-scoped the DRC Level 3 notice (page last reviewed 15 July 2026) to name Haut-Uele, Ituri, Nord-Kivu (North Kivu) and Tshopo provinces, adding the two provinces designated epidemic zones on 12 July; Sud-Kivu is no longer listed among the affected provinces. The combined DRC+Uganda Level 2 notice (https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices/level2/ebola-drc-uganda) was updated the same day to reflect the new affected-provinces list. Level unchanged at Level 3; cdc_advisory and who_status unchanged. 2026-08-04: ESCALATION TO LEVEL 4. CDC split the DRC notice into two and raised the epicentre provinces to its highest tier. A NEW Level 4 (Avoid All Travel) notice, "Ebola Bundibugyo Virus Disease in Ituri and Nord-Kivu Provinces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo" (https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices/level4/ebola-drc-provinces), now covers Ituri and Nord-Kivu, advising against all travel unless for humanitarian aid or emergency response. The existing Level 3 notice was rescoped to Haut-Uele and Tshopo only and retitled accordingly (https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices/level3/ebola-democratic-republic-of-the-congo). The combined DRC+Uganda Level 2 notice continues to cover all other DRC provinces and Uganda. All three pages are dated "Page last reviewed: August 04, 2026" and the CDC Travel Notices index lists the Level 4 as New and the Level 3 and Level 2 as Updated, all 04 August 2026 (https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices). This is the first Level 4 travel notice of the outbreak; the previous ceiling was Level 3, held since 2026-05-16. cdc_travel_notice_level and cdc_travel_notice_url updated to the Level 4 notice as the highest applicable tier; the Level 3 and Level 2 URLs are recorded here. All three notices also now carry the US entry restriction in their key points: travellers, including Americans, who have been in the DRC within 21 days of their flight will not be allowed to board commercial flights bound for the United States, and US citizens and nationals recently in Uganda or South Sudan must enter through designated airports for enhanced screening. Verified on the per-country pages directly via Chrome this run, not from the index. HAN-00530, the 17 May PHEIC and the State Department Level 4 Do Not Travel advisory are unchanged. 2026-08-05: the Department of State announced an additional $242 million for Ebola response, preparedness and humanitarian assistance, taking total direct US assistance past $512 million and nearly doubling the prior commitment; the announcement aligns with the 16 June G7 commitment of up to $500 million (State Department "Ebola Response Update: August 5, 2026", https://www.state.gov/state-department-ebola-response-updates/). Funding announcement only; no change to any advisory level. 2026-08-29: CDC Travel Health Notices re-verified directly on all three per-country pages via Chrome. Level 4 (Avoid All Travel) for Ituri and Nord-Kivu, Level 3 (Reconsider Nonessential Travel) for Haut-Uélé and Tshopo, and the combined Level 2 for the rest of DRC and Uganda are all unchanged and all still dated "Page last reviewed: August 04, 2026"; the CDC Travel Notices index agrees this run. WATCH ITEM: the Level 3 notice still names only Haut-Uélé and Tshopo, while the outbreak has been in Bas-Uélé since mid-August (3 confirmed cases and 3 of 11 health zones as of SitRep 106) and the national count reached 60 of 151 health zones across six provinces on 26 August. CDC has not re-scoped for Bas-Uélé. No level change applied.

case_status: Outbreak declared OVER by Uganda MoH 2026-07-28; WHO and Africa CDC formally declared it over 2026-08-27 after the 42-day countdown from the 16 July discharge of the last imported case; final counts 20 confirmed / 18 recovered / 2 deaths
cdc_advisory: HAN-00530 (Health Alert); enhanced travel screening from 2026-05-18
who_status: Included in joint PHEIC (2026-05-17); Uganda MoH declared the outbreak over 2026-07-28; WHO acknowledged that declaration in DON614 (1 August 2026); WHO and Africa CDC issued a joint end-of-outbreak declaration on 2026-08-27 after 42 days with no new confirmed case from the 16 July discharge of the last imported patient
notes: Initial cases imported from DRC (May 15-16); healthcare-worker cases in Kampala were contacts under follow-up per Uganda MoH (not undetected community transmission). 2026-05-27: Uganda ordered border with DRC closed "with immediate effect" for four weeks (Ebola response teams, humanitarian, cargo, security exempted, subject to mandatory 21-day isolation). Measure goes against WHO guidance, which warns closures push movement to unmonitored informal crossings. 2026-05-27: CDC raised Uganda Travel Health Notice from Level 1 (Practice Usual Precautions) to Level 2 (Practice Enhanced Precautions), per the US Embassy Kampala 28 May health alert (https://ug.usembassy.gov/health-alert-u-s-embassy-kampala-uganda-may-28-2026/). US State Department Travel Advisory for Uganda at Level 4 (Do Not Travel). US entry restrictions on non-US passport holders who travelled to Uganda in the previous 21 days (from 2026-05-22, extended to green-card holders same week); CDC Title 42 Order in effect for arrivals from Uganda. Africa CDC declared a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS) on 2026-05-18 covering both DRC and Uganda. 2026-06-15: CDC re-reviewed the Bundibugyo Travel Health Notices (both per-country pages now dated 15 June 2026) and consolidated the standalone Uganda Level 2 notice into a combined DRC+Uganda Level 2 notice at https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices/level2/ebola-drc-uganda (the old /level2/ebola-uganda URL now redirects there); Uganda level unchanged at Level 2 (Practice Enhanced Precautions). cdc_travel_notice_url updated accordingly. 2026-07-15: CDC re-reviewed the combined DRC+Uganda Level 2 notice (page last reviewed 15 July 2026); Uganda level unchanged at Level 2. 2026-07-16: WHO reported Uganda's last confirmed Ebola patient was discharged from care after testing negative twice, starting the 42-day countdown before the outbreak can be declared over (WHO DG media briefing 16 July; WHO AFRO https://www.afro.who.int/countries/uganda/news/uganda-begins-countdown-end-ebola-outbreak). Uganda holds at 20 confirmed cases / 2 deaths (15 imported from DRC, 5 local). WHO Sitrep 09 additionally tracks 1 probable Uganda case / 1 probable death. Country remains at risk of re-importation while DRC transmission continues. 2026-07-28: Uganda's Ministry of Health officially declared the 2026 Ebola outbreak OVER, Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi announcing "Today, Uganda is Ebola-free" ([Xinhua 28 July](https://english.news.cn/20260728/b8f2e1310c254e6fa74e6072b4294de6/c.html); [New Vision](https://www.newvision.co.ug/category/news/uganda-is-officially-ebola-free-minister-bary-NV_237841_072026)). The declaration came BEFORE the completion of WHO's standard 42-day countdown (last patient discharged 16 July after two negative tests); the MoH justified it on full epidemiological characterisation -- outbreak source identified, transmission chains completely reconstructed, all confirmed cases epidemiologically linked, all contacts successfully followed up, and enhanced nationwide surveillance detecting no further community transmission -- arguing the 42-day criterion need not be the sole basis when an imported outbreak is fully characterised. Final Uganda counts: 20 confirmed cases (15 imported from DRC, 5 local), 18 recoveries, 2 deaths. Baryomunsi warned Ebola remains a threat while transmission continues in neighbouring DRC; Uganda will maintain surveillance and border-district preparedness. CDC Travel Notice unchanged this run: the combined DRC+Uganda Level 2 notice (https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices/level2/ebola-drc-uganda) still reads Level 2 for Uganda, page last reviewed 15 July 2026 (CDC has not yet reflected the declaration). WHO formal end-of-outbreak concurrence not yet issued as of this run. 2026-08-01: WHO formally acknowledged Uganda's end-of-outbreak declaration in [Disease Outbreak News DON614](https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2026-DON614), and in doing so corrected this tracker's earlier reading that Uganda declared ahead of the 42-day window. WHO's account is that the declaration followed 42 days with no new confirmed locally transmitted case, counting from the discharge of the last locally transmitted case on 16 June 2026; the 16 July discharge was of the most recent IMPORTED case, and WHO is running a separate 42-day monitoring period from that date. So the 42-day criterion on local transmission was met, and the residual clock covers importation, not local chains. WHO reiterates that Uganda remains at risk of re-importation while transmission continues in DR Congo and calls for heightened surveillance and preparedness. This is WHO acknowledgement, not yet a WHO end-of-outbreak concurrence statement of its own. 2026-08-02: CDC Travel Health Notices re-verified via Chrome on the per-country pages; the combined DRC+Uganda Level 2 notice still covers Uganda and non-affected DRC provinces, page last reviewed 15 July 2026. CDC has still not reflected the 28 July declaration. Level unchanged. 2026-08-04: CDC updated the combined DRC+Uganda Level 2 notice (page last reviewed 04 August 2026) as part of the same restructuring that created the new DRC Level 4 notice for Ituri and Nord-Kivu. Uganda's level is UNCHANGED at Level 2 (Practice Enhanced Precautions) and Uganda remains named in the notice title and key points, so CDC has still not reflected Uganda's 28 July end-of-outbreak declaration eight days on. The notice now also carries the US entry restriction language: US citizens and nationals recently in Uganda or South Sudan, and not in DRC, must enter the United States through designated airports for enhanced screening. Verified on the per-country page directly via Chrome this run. 2026-08-27: WHO AND AFRICA CDC FORMALLY DECLARE THE UGANDA OUTBREAK OVER. In a joint news release from Addis Ababa, Brazzaville and Geneva, Africa CDC and WHO welcomed the end of the Bundibugyo outbreak in Uganda following 42 consecutive days with no new confirmed case, counting from the discharge of the country's last patient, an imported case, on 16 July 2026 ([WHO AFRO, 27 August 2026](https://www.afro.who.int/countries/uganda/news/uganda-ends-ebola-outbreak-following-completion-42-day-countdown)). This closes the residual importation clock that DON614 described on 1 August and converts WHO's earlier acknowledgement of Uganda's 28 July self-declaration into a WHO end-of-outbreak concurrence of its own. The release restates the final counts this tracker has carried unchanged since 28 July: 20 confirmed cases (15 imported from DRC, 5 locally acquired among contacts and health workers linked to imported cases), 18 recoveries, 2 deaths, more than 800 contacts identified and monitored, outbreak declared 15 May 2026. Quoted: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus (WHO DG), Jean Kaseya (Africa CDC DG) and Mohamed Janabi (WHO Regional Director for Africa), all framing the milestone against continuing transmission in DRC and the resulting re-importation risk. WHO reiterates its standing advice against travel and trade restrictions and against suspending flights, closing borders or denying entry to travellers from affected countries. No timeseries or country_breakdown figure changes: Uganda's 20 / 2 / 18 were already final. DATE DISCREPANCY NOTED: [ECDC](https://www.ecdc.europa.eu/en/ebola-outbreak-democratic-republic-congo-and-uganda) dates the WHO declaration to 26 August; the WHO AFRO release itself is published and modified 27 August 2026, and the WHO date is taken here. 2026-08-29: CDC Travel Health Notices re-verified directly on all three per-country pages via Chrome (not the index). Level 4 Ituri and Nord-Kivu, Level 3 Haut-Uélé and Tshopo, Level 2 combined DRC-and-Uganda, all three still dated "Page last reviewed: August 04, 2026". Uganda remains named in the Level 2 notice title and key points, so CDC has still not reflected either the 28 July Uganda declaration or the 27 August WHO/Africa CDC close-out. No level change; cdc_travel_notice_level and cdc_travel_notice_url unchanged.
